title: Impact anchors — one-pager + manager prep
content:
Purpose: quick single-sheet I can drop into 1:1s and calibration conversations. Focus is alignment on where I should spend time next 90 days (high-impact, measurable), plus concise evidence so manager can signal support/objections quickly.

TL;DR:
- Primary anchor: reduce new-hire time-to-productivity for eng and SE by 25% over Q2 (measure: time to first PR merged + first support ticket resolved).
- Secondary anchor: improve onboarding feedback NPS (first-week survey) from 3.6 -> 4.3.
- Org health anchor: run 3 inclusive onboarding experiments (mentorship pairing, micro-docs, buddy rotations) and surface results with cost/effort.

Why this matters (one sentence each):
- Faster ramp improves product velocity and lowers recruiter/ops overhead; clear ROI tied to headcount cadence.
- Better early experience reduces first-90 attrition risk and increases referral likelihood.
- A/B experiments let us pick pragmatic, low-cost fixes instead of big monolithic rebuilds.

Signals / evidence I can point to today:
- Current metric baseline: median time to first merged PR = 21 days (data: onboarding-metrics Q1 export).
- First-week survey response rate 42%, mean 3.6 free-form comments trending around "missing runbook" and "unclear expectations".
- Anecdotal: two mid-SD hires escalated onboarding blockers on day 8 -> engineering time lost (refs: slack thread #onboarding-escals, PRs linked).
- Recent pilot: micro-docs reduced a tracked blocker from 6h -> 1.5h for two hires (pilot notes attached).

Planned experiments (priority order):
1) Buddy rotations (2-week pairs) — lightweight, test on next 4 hires. Metric: reduction in blocker reopen rate. Est effort: 0.5 PM day + ops automation.
2) First-week micro-checklist + quick videos (5 topics) — convert top-5 questions into 10-min assets. Metric: survey NPS lift. Est effort: 3 engineer hours each + one content sprint.
3) PR triage mini-SLA (assign reviewer within 48h) — requires reviewer dip policy and small incentive. Metric: time to first merged PR.

Manager prep bullets (what I want you to know / ask in 1:1):
- I think biggest leverage is lowering friction in the first 14 days; I want permission to run buddy rotations on 4 hires (low-risk) and to use 2 headcount hours for micro-doc creation.
- Trade-offs: prioritizing onboarding ops now means delaying broader LMS migration planning by ~3 weeks. Is that OK given current roadmap?
- Support ask: help unblock hiring manager alignment for scheduling buddy windows and a quick signal on incentive for reviewers.

Concrete asks (pick 1):
- Say yes to small pilot (4 hires) for buddy rotations, or
- If not, give specific reason (capacity/priority) so I can re-prioritize to micro-docs only.

Risks / concerns:
- Low survey response can bias signal; mitigation: tie micro-checklist to onboarding flow to boost response via in-product prompt.
- Reviewer incentives may be perceived as unfair; mitigation: rotate reviewers and track time impact, keep it transparent.

Quick wins map (30/60/90):
- 30d: launch buddy rotation pilot with 2 live pairs, publish first-week checklist, capture baseline metrics.
- 60d: iterate on micro-docs, onboard 2 additional hires into pilot, measure PR merge delta.
- 90d: consolidate results, recommendation memo (go/no-go), and run a short cross-functional review with Eng Managers + Recruiting.

Notes / rough timeline / TO-DOs:
- TODO: sync with Carlos to wire up metrics export from onboarding-metrics (JIRA-POPS-1123).
- TODO: draft 5 micro-video scripts (Ava to review for clarity).
- Calendar: add 15m sync with Hiring Managers 2026-03-08 to get buy-in.
- Draft comms: short email template to hiring manager announcing buddy rotations (keep expectations explicit).

Evidence snippets to cite in 1:1 (short quotes I can read aloud):
- "Blocked on missing runbook — spent 6 hours debugging deploy flow" (new hire X, day 7).
- "First-week checklist would have saved me at least 2 meetings" (survey free-form).
- Pilot result: micro-doc reduced blocker resolution time by ~75% for two hires (pilot notes dated 2026-02-09).

Open questions for manager during calibration / review:
- Given Q2 roadmap: if we show a 25% improvement in time-to-productivity, do we get formal headcount/time credits for onboarding team to scale the solution?
- Preference for experiment cadence: run all three in parallel small-scale, or serially with quick learn loops?

Fallbacks if pilot fails:
- If buddy rotation adoption <50%: pivot to documented office hours + recorded answers.
- If PR SLA not feasible: focus on owner calendars + triage days (weekly).

Appendix: relevant links (placeholders I will swap in before 1:1):
- onboarding-metrics export: CONFLUENCE-hr-growth-2026
- pilot notes: docs/onboarding/pilot-2026-02-09

Tone notes: keep this short in the meeting, use the anchors to structure discussion; avoid too much process detail unless asked.

Last quick reflection: this is intentionally operational and measurable — want the manager to be able to say yes/no quickly. If yes: next doc will be a short execution checklist with clear owners. If no: capture constraints and move to plan B.
